A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FluidNexus and contain complete, readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Supplementary Material A-F. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, prediction, re-simulation, and interaction experiments, including quantitative benchmarks, ablations, and supplementary multi-view results (Tables 1-4 and S1).

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments on ScalarFlow, FluidNexus-Smoke, and FluidNexus-Ball, together with ablations and supplementary evaluations (Tables 1-4 and S1).

M1.justification: The diffusion pipeline, two particle sets, losses, and reconstruction/prediction procedures remain unchanged (Section 3; Algorithms S1-S2). Renaming the representation from 'two-layer' to 'visual-physical' and explaining its motivation do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three datasets and the same reconstruction, prediction, re-simulation, and interaction scenarios. Appendix E retains the same in-the-wild and multi-view evaluations.

E2.justification: PINF, HyFluid, and SpacetimeGaussians remain the comparators in Tables 1-3 and S1. Interaction experiments still compare only against SpacetimeGaussians (Section 4.2); no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The train/test splits, camera inputs, held-out views, frame budgets, preprocessing, model configurations, and evaluation metrics are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C-E.

E4.justification: Table 4, Figure 9, and Appendix F retain the same video-generation and physics-loss ablations. The supplementary in-the-wild and multi-view analyses are also unchanged; Figure 9's image downsampling does not introduce a different analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and S1 retain identical result entries and numerical values, and the reported rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged. Figures 4 and 9 show the same examples despite reduced embedded-image resolution.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and derivations remain unchanged, including Equations 1-9 and S1-S5. The added sentence in Section 3.2 supplies conceptual motivation rather than a new formal assumption or mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-video fluid reconstruction and prediction, integration of generative models with physics, and the two new datasets.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains why separate particle sets are needed: velocity is defined throughout ambient 3D space, whereas visible-fluid appearance occupies particular regions. Existing result interpretations and limitations, including blurry detail and limited generalization, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Model choices, fine-tuning schedules, data-processing instructions, simulation parameters, timing information, and project-access disclosures are unchanged (Section 4; Appendices B-D). The added design rationale supplies no new implementation instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference 61 changes its year/volume metadata from '36, 2024' to '2023' but still identifies the same HyFluid paper.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'two-layer' with 'visual-physical' terminology, adds a short design explanation, and makes limited paragraph, header, and bibliographic edits. The overall section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure S1's particle labels and caption, and Figure 2's caption, adopt the revised terminology. Figures 4 and 9 retain their panels but use downsampled images. Minor text reflow occurs without adding, removing, or reorganizing figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The added rationale in Section 3.2 and more descriptive particle terminology make the existing design easier to understand. Downsampling Figures 4 and 9 reduces detail when enlarged, but their qualitative comparisons remain readable. The net gain is limited to explanatory clarity; the scientific claims, methods, and empirical support are unchanged.
